modelingNotes: Alignment, cornice outline (50.4 x 28.1 m) and wall body (47.4 x 24.6 m) from the OSM minimum rectangle and building:part polygons (way 226413508); the 1.5/1.8 m cornice overhang is the OSM difference between them.
Four sculpture pedestals (8.2 m wide, 1.8 m projection, 6 m high) and the 8.4 m transverse passage width follow the mapped parts.

Published dimensions (Wikipedia FR/EN, Structurae): 49.5-50 m high, main arch 29.19 m high x 14.62 m wide, transverse arches 18.68 m high x 8.44 m wide. Total height kept at the exported 50 m (roof pavilion top).
Main arch width set to 14.0 m: OSM maps 12 m, the published 14.62 m is on a 44.8 m body; the front photograph gives arch/body ~0.29, which on the OSM 47.4 m body is 14 m, leaving 16.7 m piers.

Storey lines scaled from the reviewed front photograph (00.jpg) on the 50 m height: plinth 1.5 m, dado 5.4-6.0 m, transverse impost 14.5 m, main impost entablature 20.5-22.2 m, upper relief panels 25-31.6 m, architrave 33.9 m, frieze 34.8-37.6 m, main cornice 37.6-41.4 m, attic 41.4-46.8 m, attic cornice to 48.0 m, palmette cresting to 49.35 m.
Attic: 30 shields (11 per main face, 4 per side) between sword panels, counted from the photographs.

Sculpture groups, spandrel Fames, upper panels and the frieze are abstract relief masses (lathed figure blocks, wing slabs, raised blocks), not copies of the sculptures. The coffered vaults are rib grids with rosettes.

The roof is a flat terrace behind the attic parapet; the OSM 47-50 m rooftop parts are reduced to a small set-back stair/lift kiosk (4.4 x 3.2 m, top 50.0 m) invisible from street level. Pier and upper walls carry thin raised ashlar coursing bands every 0.95 m; the dentil course sits under the modillions.

assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Plan and heights from OSM way 56185523 and its 8 building:parts: 20 m stone halls (entablature/parapet at 16.3-18.9 m), 19 m colonnade strip, 25 m porch and inner hall, glazed barrel nave and transept (eave 25 m, crown 42 m), crossing dome (mapped circle r 36.4 m, top 50 m) and the octagonal rotunda of the Palais de la Decouverte. The model is built in a frame fitted to the mapped nave rectangle (bearing 4.4 deg).

Researched (fr.wikipedia Grand Palais): nave 200 m x 50 m plus apses (240 m overall), 35 m under the ironwork, 45 m under the dome, 60 m to the top of the lantern; pale reseda-green painted ironwork; mosaic frieze 3.2 m high behind the colonnade; two quadrigas by Georges Recipon (Immortality outrunning Time, Champs-Elysees end; Harmony triumphing over Discord, Seine end) on the corner pavilions of the main facade. Wikipedia records two quadrigas, so two are modelled (not four). The lantern and flagpole were raised to the published 60 m (previous export: 56 m).

Inferred from the Commons photographs (bundle references 00-05): the nave ends are glazed half-domes (22 m long) inside the mapped rectangle; 16 Ionic columns per side colonnade (3.9 m spacing, 10.6 m shafts on a 3 m podium), arched windows and the mosaic band on the gallery wall, balustrade with urns over every column; central porch of 6 giant columns (single-pair-pair-single, 18 m) before three arched doorways; two pylons with paired columns, a tall window and a sculpture group; the green iron arch and glazed lunette of the transept above the porch. Sculpture is represented by abstract masses.

Ironwork is a simplified grid in the patina finish (the library has no reseda paint): transverse arched trusses every ~9 m, glazing bars, horizontal purlins that wrap round the apses, apse meridians, 16 dome meridians with rings, crown walkways. The Palais de la Decouverte (west wing) gets pilastered bays, its Avenue Franklin-Roosevelt entrance with paired columns and a small entrance rotunda dome (position and size inferred), and the mapped octagon as a ribbed glazed dome (apex lowered to 40 m with a 42 m lantern ring instead of the mapped pyramid).

modelingNotes: Plan from OSM (outline + 63 building:part polygons). Local axis fitted to the mapped entablature rectangle (102.3 x 43.3 m, bearing 25.6 deg); cella (way 1459282734, antae and front pilasters), podium with the four stair cheek walls (4.4 m), the two-flight stairs with landings at both ends (2.2/4.4 m) are extruded from the mapped polygons; all 54 mapped column centroids are kept (8 + 8 in the double south pronaos row, 15 per side, 8 north).

Heights from the mapped IGN LiDAR HD tags: podium 4.4 m, column tops 24.2 m, eaves ~28 m, pediment apex 36.2 m (kept as exported). Published: columns ~20 m high (mapped 19.8 m), temple 108 x 43 m (Wikipedia).

Entablature 24.2-28.0 m (architrave with 3 fasciae, relief frieze, dentil band, modillion cornice) and pediment slope (18.4 deg) proportioned from the reviewed south-front photograph (00.jpg); podium is lower than the ~7 m often quoted because the mapped LiDAR terrace is 4.4 m.

Columns: Attic base on plinth, 12-flute entasis shaft (1.84 m base diameter), two-tier acanthus bell, concave abacus. Cella: ashlar coursing, plinth, antae and pilaster capitals, top panel band; 34 statue niches (14 per side between the columns as in 04.jpg, 2 flanking the south door as in 00.jpg, 4 on the north wall - north count inferred).

South bronze doors (Triqueti, ~10.4 x 5 m) as bronze relief panels in a trim surround with console cornice; south tympanum carries abstract masses for Lemaire's Last Judgement (Christ centre, Magdalene kneeling, angels, the saved and the damned); north tympanum plain. Frieze: relief blocks and the D.O.M. SUB INVOC. S. M. MAGDALENAE tablet on the south front (letters as blocks).

Roof: mapped gable (copper tag; rendered as grey metal roof) with standing seams, hidden behind a blocking course and the pediments; three low zinc drums with glazed oculi mark the three interior domes (positions inferred from the three nave bays). Peristyle ceiling beams at every column; bronze railings between the side columns (04.jpg).
Sculpture, capitals' leaves, coffering and relief detail are abstracted; statues are simple masses.

assets.name: Opéra Garnier
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Plan: the saved OSM footprint and the eleven mapped building:part ways. The model is authored in a frame rotated 15.6 deg to the facade edge of way/822290986 and rotated back, so every volume stays on the OSM plan.

Heights from OSM parts: side wings 26 m (986), main block walls 31 m with a 4 m copper roof to 35 m (002), rotunda drums 29 m with 7.5 m domes (989-991), auditorium drum 31-44 m (987), dome 44-51 m (1001), crown 50-56.5 m (1000) and finial to 58 m (993), fly tower from 31 m (992).

Fly tower: OSM gives 58 m with a 10 m gabled roof; here the eaves are 46 m and the gable apex 54.9 m so the Apollo group on the apex tops out at the mapped 58 m (the model top stays 58 m; the 70 m outline tag is unused).

South front researched against the Commons references 00/01 and published figures (facade ~32 m high, gilded Harmony and Poetry groups ~7.5 m tall, Wikipedia "Palais Garnier"). Bay rhythm is read from the OSM footprint steps: 7 arches at u = 0, +-7.1, +-14.3 (centre) and +-22.55 (end pavilions), piers 2.7 m wide.

Elevation levels inferred from photo proportions scaled to the mapped widths: arcade springing 5.3 m, loggia floor 9.6 m, 16 paired Corinthian columns 10.8-20.6 m (r 0.48 m), small loggia columns to 16.2 m, oculi with busts at 18.7 m, entablature 20.6-22.8 m, attic to 29.2 m, gilded cresting to 31 m.

Side facades: two storeys of round-arched windows between pilasters, attic lights and cornice at 26 m, interpreted from general views; the Pavillon de l'Empereur ramp is a simplified double ramp hugging the west rotunda within 2 m of the plan.

Fly tower articulation (inferred from general views): corner buttresses, 7 pilastered bays per side with a lower arcade of glazed panels, arched windows and attic lights, storey/attic bands and cornice, double raking cornices on both gables, copper roof with 9 standing seams and a ridge crest, rearing Pegasus masses (copper-patina bronze) on the rear corners.

Roofscape: copper hipped roofs with ridges over the side-wing strips, rotunda wings, rear blocks and the 35 m terraces, plus small skylight lanterns; long side facades get a projecting central avant-corps with a raised attic.

Roofs: copper mansard slopes on the 31-35 m main block, a copper foyer ridge, a copper-roofed lantern over the grand staircase (inferred size) and a copper skirt round the drum; flat terraces use the cool roof swatch. The east rotunda axis is nudged 0.6 m west of part 990 so its cornice stays within the jagged OSM outline.

Sculpture (the four ground-floor groups, the gilded roof groups, Apollo, busts, masks, medallions) is represented by original abstract masses; gold uses the library "invalides-gold" finish in the terracotta slot, copper roofs use "copper" in the metal slot. No sculpture replicas, textures or Mapbox geometry.

assets.name: Basilique du Sacré-Cœur
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Plan registration: every mass is built from, or centred on, the mapped OSM building:part polygons (outline, Greek-cross arms, four corner-dome towers, choir, ambulatory, apse, south porch, gable, equestrian plinths, turrets and campanile).

Mapped heights retained: 16 m perimeter body, 24 m arm walls with 33 m roof ridges, 33 m corner drums, 46 m corner domes with lanterns to 53 m, 73 m main dome with lantern cross to 83 m, 57/64 m campanile square stage and 84 m campanile top.

Main dome: drum 31-48.5 m rising behind the 33 m roof ridges (arcaded exterior colonnade of 16 bays, attic with 32 small arched windows), tall pointed ovoid dome springing at 48.45 m (r 9.9 m, 22 m semi-axis, stepped stone courses) reaching the mapped 70 m lantern base; slim colonnaded lantern with cross to the mapped 83 m. Drum/dome split inferred from the south-facade photograph.

Corner domes: octagonal drums (24-33 m) with paired arched windows under one archivolt, pointed ovoid coursed domes reaching the mapped 46 m, slim open lanterns and crosses to 53 m (OSM gives no roof:height; profile inferred from photographs).
Campanile: square shaft with corner buttresses and slit windows, three-arched belfry per face, parapet at 57 m, 12-bay arcaded drum, ovoid dome and lantern with cross reaching the mapped 84 m.

South facade: three tall vaulted arches (spring 6.4 m, crown ~8.8 m) filling the mapped porch plan between the two mapped 13 m end piers, which carry simplified equestrian statue masses (St Louis and Joan of Arc, patina), upper three-arched loggia, triangular gable with Christ niche aedicule and two domed turrets.

Arm roofs are low stone gables meeting at the crossing, the chevet steps up from eight radiating chapels with coursed domelets on the 16 m terrace, to the 24 m ambulatory terrace, to a windowed semicircular apse clerestory (to 28.6 m) under a coursed half-dome meeting the 33 m ridge; roofs are pale stone as on the building. Transept gable ends carry raking cornices and a traceried rose (moulded ring, spokes, hub, glass behind); the square bases of the corner towers carry the large arched niches with roses seen on the south front; small domed pinnacles ring the chevet on the ambulatory (count/spacing inferred, ~6 m).
Windows: round-arched with stone surrounds on the 16 m body and 24 m clerestory; bay spacing (~4.5-5 m) is inferred from photographs.
Omitted: sculpture, mosaics, bells, fine masonry, the terrace and steps. Statues are schematic horse-and-rider masses.

assets.name: Église Saint-Roch
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: OSM: the saved footprint (chapels, transept arms, apse, Lady Chapel ring, rear chapels) and three parts (cross-gabled nave, apse, dome at the Lady Chapel). OSM gives no heights; the published total is kept at the earlier 30 m top (Lady Chapel lantern).

Registration: model authored in a frame rotated -33.8 deg onto the Rue Saint-Honore facade edge and rotated back, walls built from the footprint set back 0.45 m so cornices stay inside the mapped outline; facade projections are clipped to the jagged front edge (pavilion projects 1.9 m, wings are engaged).

Facade researched from the Commons reference 00.jpg and Wikipedia "Eglise Saint-Roch" (facade of 1736 by Robert de Cotte, completed by Jules-Robert de Cotte, two superposed orders, Doric/Corinthian). Elevation read from the photo: 8 lower columns and 3 doors, upper storey 4 free columns + pilasters, clock window and arch, scroll buttresses, statues on the end pedestals, curved pediment cartouche and cross. Vertical proportions stretched ~12% so the pediment apex is 25.7 m and the cross 27.7 m (below the 30 m Lady Chapel top).

Inferred: nave/transept eaves 18 m and ridges 23 m, chapel eaves 9.5 m with lean-to roofs, six clerestory bays per side, Lady Chapel drum and ovoid dome to a 30 m lantern, rear chapels 9.5 m with mansard roofs. Sculpture is abstract masses only.
